notes.q: Which dam formed Lake Hamilton, and when was it completed?
notes.text: Arkansas Power & Light developed the lake; Carpenter Dam, a concrete gravity dam, was completed in 1931 and the lake was created in 1932.

notes.q: About how many acres is Lake Hamilton?
notes.text: Wikipedia gives Lake Hamilton as 7,200 acres; Lake Catherine, the smaller of the two lakes, is about 1,940 acres.

notes.q: Which dam forms Lake Catherine, and when was it built?
notes.text: Both Remmel and Carpenter dams were listed on the National Register in 1992.

notes.q: What type of dam is Lake Catherine's Remmel Dam?
notes.text: It was built in 1924 by Ford, Bacon & Davis with Ambursen Construction.

notes.q: Which dam creates Lake Ouachita near Hot Springs?
notes.text: The Army Corps of Engineers built the 231-ft dam from 1948 to 1953.

notes.q: About how many islands does Lake Ouachita have?
notes.text: Wikipedia's infobox lists 200 islands for the lake.

notes.q: Which historic healing springs does Lake Ouachita State Park preserve?
notes.text: The 360-acre park opened in 1955.

notes.q: On which river is DeGray Lake, south of Hot Springs?
notes.text: The dam is approximately eight miles above the river's confluence with the Ouachita River.

notes.q: According to Wikipedia, DeGray Lake holds the distinction as the first Corps of Engineers impoundment able to do what?
notes.text: Wikipedia calls it the first "pump back capable" impoundment in the history of the Corps of Engineers.

notes.q: What is DeGray Lake's maximum depth?
notes.text: Its average depth is about 47 ft.

notes.q: What is the Arkansas state-record walleye, and where was it caught?
notes.text: It was caught at Greers Ferry Lake on March 12, 1982.

notes.q: What is Arkansas's statewide daily limit for black bass?
notes.text: The possession limit is triple the daily limit.
notes.source: AGFC: Statewide lengths and daily limits

notes.q: What is Arkansas's statewide daily crappie limit?
notes.text: Black and white crappie are combined in the limit; area-specific rules may differ.
notes.source: AGFC: Statewide lengths and daily limits

notes.q: What is the Arkansas state-record striped bass?
notes.text: AGFC lists it as caught at Beaver Lake Tailwater on 04/28/2000.

notes.q: Why must Lake Ouachita's striped bass be stocked every year?
notes.text: AGFC says striped bass do not reproduce naturally in the wild, apart from one Arkansas River population; Lake Ouachita is one of four lakes it stocks.
notes.source: Arkansas Game & Fish Commission: Striped Bass

notes.q: What tree did AGFC and the Corps mostly use for new Lake Ouachita fish brush piles?
notes.text: AGFC said the brush piles would sit in the 20- to 25-foot range most of the year, on points near the mid-lake islands.
notes.source: AGFC: Improving angling odds at Lake Ouachita

notes.q: What lure caught the 11-lb Lake Hamilton largemouth at a May 2024 club tournament?
notes.text: The color was Green Pumpkin Magic.
notes.source: AGFC: Tourney anglers catch a couple of whopper bass in Lake Hamilton

notes.q: How many acres is Garvan Woodland Gardens on Lake Hamilton?
notes.text: The University of Arkansas owns the garden.

notes.q: What does the name of novaculite, the Ouachita whetstone rock, mean in Latin?
notes.text: Novaculite takes its name from the Latin for "razor stone."

notes.q: What two industry grades are Garland County novaculite whetstones sold as?
notes.text: "Washita" is duller and porous; "Arkansas" is finer-grained, waxy and denser.

notes.q: Into which lake does Hot Springs Creek empty after flowing under Bathhouse Row?
notes.text: Wikipedia says the creek flows from Whittington Avenue through the southern city before emptying into Lake Hamilton.

notes.q: Which rock found around Hot Springs is used to make Arkansas whetstones?
notes.text: The Arkansas Geological Survey calls novaculite a recrystallized variety of chert made of very small quartz grains.

notes.q: Which fish does the AGFC stock from November through April in the Ouachita River tailwaters below Carpenter Dam?
notes.text: The AGFC stocks catchable rainbow trout there to take advantage of cooler water temperatures.

notes.q: Which Arkansas state fish hatchery sits on Lake Hamilton?
notes.text: The entry places it on the south side of Lake Hamilton, which is also its water source.
notes.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission State Fish Hatcheries

notes.q: Eagle-watch cruises at Lake Ouachita State Park in January and February look for which bird?
notes.text: Per the Democrat-Gazette, Lake Ouachita State Park runs eagle-watch cruises in winter, and DeGray Lake holds its Eagles Et Cetera festival.
notes.source: Arkansas Democrat-Gazette: Eagle-watching excursions take off at state parks (2019)

notes.q: Which month is the wettest in Hot Springs on average?
notes.text: Wikipedia says rainfall is highest in May, which averages about 6.5 inches.

notes.q: What is Hot Springs' record high temperature?
notes.text: It was reached in 1936 and again in 1986.

notes.q: About how much snow does Hot Springs average per year?
notes.text: Wikipedia's climate table lists average annual snowfall of 1.1 inches.

notes.q: About how long is the Ouachita River, which is dammed into Lakes Ouachita, Hamilton and Catherine?
notes.text: It rises in Polk County and joins the Tensas in Louisiana.

notes.q: Which oak grows naturally at only four sites in the world, all in the Ouachita Mountains?
notes.text: The maple-leaf oak (Quercus acerifolia) is found at only four sites worldwide, all of them in the Ouachitas.
